Row.Text: No other civilization you know of has formed a new nation.
Your civilization has no formable nations in this version.

Partners keep their own governments. Each bond has a cohesion score shown on the Unions tab: shared religion, trade and your Influence lead strengthen it; rivals, wars and unhappiness erode it. Low cohesion brings autonomy crises and, at worst, secession. War with a partner ends the bond at once.
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Not possible in this world:[ENDCOLOR] {1_Group} does not exist in this game.
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]The moment has passed:[ENDCOLOR] this can only be proclaimed up to the {1_Era}.
Hold the {1_Stage} for {2_Num} turns ({3_Held} so far)
Price of peaceful annexation: {1_Num} [ICON_GOLD] Gold (you have {2_Have})
The {1_Stage} of {2_Leader} has dissolved: its partners are no longer bound to the crown.
You can now proclaim the {1_Stage}. Open Formable Nations from the information menu at the top right.
+2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.

In 1385 Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agreed at Krewo to marry Jadwiga, Queen of Poland, and to accept Catholic baptism for himself and his realm. Crowned Wladyslaw II Jagiello in 1386, he ruled both crowns as one dynasty while each kept its own state.
+1 Delegate in the World Congress. +5% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. Wheat: +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

The Union of Lublin (1569) turned the dynastic union into a single Commonwealth of Both Nations, with an elected king and a common Sejm. Its nobility's "Golden Liberty" made it one of the most widely enfranchised states of its age, until the partitions ended it in 1795.
+5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +25% Influence from gifts of [ICON_GOLD] Gold to City-States.

When King Louis II fell at Mohacs in 1526, his brother-in-law Ferdinand of Habsburg was elected to the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary. The Habsburg lands remained a composite monarchy of separate kingdoms bound by one dynasty for more than three centuries.

+5% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +5% [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. Opera Houses: +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. A City-State joined to you by dynastic marriage satisfies the claim and keeps its own government.
The Compromise of 1867 split the Austrian Empire into two partner states under one monarch, sharing an army, foreign policy and finance. The Dual Monarchy lasted until 1918.

In 962 Pope John XII crowned Otto I emperor in Rome. The Empire that followed was no single state but an elective union of princes, bishoprics and free cities from the North Sea to the Italian peninsula, and endured until 1806.
+5% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production. +10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of military units. +15% yields from internal trade routes (the Zollverein).
On 18 January 1871 the German Empire was proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, uniting Prussia with Saxony, Bavaria and the other German states under the Prussian king as emperor.
+2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In 1603 James VI of Scotland inherited the throne of England as James I. For a century the two kingdoms shared a monarch but kept their own parliaments, churches and laws.
+5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +1 [ICON_MOVES] Movement for embarked units. Harbors: +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
The Acts of Union of 1707 merged the kingdoms of England and Scotland, and their parliaments, into the single Kingdom of Great Britain.
You lead no union. Proclaim a union on the Nations tab to bind partners to your crown.
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]At this rate, secession risk in about {1_Num} turns.[ENDCOLOR]
How they feel treated as a vassal

[COLOR_YELLOW]Autonomy crisis.[ENDCOLOR] Concede ({1_Gold} [ICON_GOLD] now), grant privileges ({2_Tribute} [ICON_GOLD] per turn for a while), or assert crown authority (-{3_Influence} Influence with every other City-State). Unanswered, the crisis lapses with no effect.
An autonomy crisis has broken out in {1_Partner}, part of your {2_Union}. Respond on the Unions tab of Formable Nations.
{1_Partner} is moving to break away from {2_Leader}. Unless the union recovers, it will secede in {3_Num} turns.
The independence movement in {1_Partner} has lost momentum. The union holds.
[COLOR_GREY]Functional organisation: one shared purpose; members join and leave freely.[ENDCOLOR]
[COLOR_GREY]Intergovernmental organisation: sovereign members cooperating on many fronts.[ENDCOLOR]
Your income from membership last turn: {1_Num} [ICON_GOLD] Gold
Willing founding members now: {1_Num} (needs {2_Need}, including you). Other human players are invited after founding.
Not enough willing members yet (City-States must be your Friends; AI leaders must not be hostile)
You are invited to join the {1_Org}. Accept on the Organisations tab of Formable Nations.
Open borders between member civilizations. +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each of your trade routes to another member. +1 Influence per turn with each member City-State.
+3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each of your trade routes to another member. +1 Influence per turn with each member City-State. Members need a coastal capital. Dissolves after the Renaissance.

From the 13th to the 17th century, merchant guilds and market towns around the Baltic and North Sea, led by Luebeck, protected their trade together, with foreign offices (Kontore) in Bruges, Bergen, London and Novgorod.
Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
+1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each [ICON_RES_OIL] Oil you own (up to 10). Open to anyone owning at least 2 Oil.
Founded in Baghdad in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela to coordinate oil policy among producing countries.
Founded in Cairo in March 1945 by Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria, with Yemen joining that May.
The Organisation of African Unity was founded in Addis Ababa in 1963. It was replaced by the African Union in 2002.
Founded with the Bangkok Declaration of 8 August 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
Founded in 1952 by Denmark, Iceland, Norway and Sweden; Finland joined in 1955.
The Southern Common Market was created by the Treaty of Asuncion in 1991 by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
[COLOR_YELLOW]On proclamation:[ENDCOLOR] a [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age of {1_Num} turns.
Stronger than the Knight (+2 [ICON_STRENGTH]) and starts with Charge. Available while you hold the Holy Roman Empire.

The Imperial Knights (Reichsritter) were free nobles who held their lands directly from the emperor rather than from any prince, and owed him service in the saddle. Their independence lasted until the Empire itself ended in 1806.
Stronger than the Musketman (+2 [ICON_RANGE_STRENGTH] Ranged Strength) and starts with Cover I. Available while you hold the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Hungarian-style infantry with matchlocks and sabres, the haiduks became the core of the Commonwealth's foot soldiers under Stefan Batory in the 1570s and later served as guards of the king and the great magnates.
Stronger than the Rifleman (+2 [ICON_STRENGTH]) and starts with Charge. Available while you hold the Kingdom of Great Britain.

The Black Watch, raised in 1739, was the first of the Highland regiments of the British Army. Recruited from the Scottish Highlands, they kept their own dress and pipers and served in every major British campaign that followed.
Stronger than the Great War Infantry (+3 [ICON_STRENGTH]) and starts with Drill I. Available while you hold Austria-Hungary.

The Imperial Rifles (Kaiserschuetzen) were the Austro-Hungarian mountain infantry of Tyrol and Vorarlberg. In the First World War they held the high Alpine front against Italy, fighting at altitudes of over 3,000 metres.
Stronger than the Lancer (+2 [ICON_STRENGTH]) and starts with Sentry (+1 Sight). Available while you hold the German Empire.
Lancer regiments of Polish-Lithuanian origin, uhlans were adopted across Europe. In the German Empire's wars they were used above all for scouting and screening ahead of the main army.

Colonies on other landmasses and cities of other peoples are not yet part of your nation. Each has a local cohesion score. Below 35 an independence movement forms; below 20 the city counts down to independence. Held at 75 or more for 30 turns, a city integrates for good. Your capital, your home landmass and City-States joined peacefully never break away.
All your cities are integrated into your nation.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Integrates in {1_Num} turns if cohesion stays at 75 or more.[ENDCOLOR]
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Breaks away in {1_Num} turns unless cohesion rises to 20.[ENDCOLOR]
[COLOR_YELLOW]Ready to break away, but it cannot yet: too early in history, or another city broke away recently.[ENDCOLOR]

[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]An independence movement is under way.[ENDCOLOR] Grant autonomy ({1_Cost} [ICON_GOLD] Gold, +15 for 20 turns), suppress it (needs a garrison; +20 for 10 turns, but the city falls into resistance for {2_Turns} turns), or grant independence: the city goes in peace and starts friendly toward you.
An independence movement has formed in {1_City}. Respond on the Provinces tab of Formable Nations.
{1_City} will break away from {2_Owner} in {3_Num} turns unless its cohesion recovers.
{1_City} is now an integral part of your nation and will never seek independence.
{1_City} has declared independence from {2_Owner} as the City-State of {3_New}.
{2_Owner} has granted independence to {1_City}, now the City-State of {3_New}.
Restless neighbouring cities went with it: {1_Num}.
[COLOR_YELLOW]Supranational:[ENDCOLOR] shared rules bind the members. Each member's commitment is measured by its cohesion with the organisation; a member that loses faith holds an exit referendum.
It has merged into its successor.
Only a member of the organisation it grows out of can found it.
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]An exit referendum will be held in {1_Num} turns.[ENDCOLOR] Negotiating opt-outs ({2_Cost} [ICON_GOLD] Gold) calls it off and adds +15 cohesion for 20 turns.
Ideology compared with the leading member
Declaration of friendship with a member
The {1_Org} has been merged into the {2_Org}.
{1_Member} will hold a referendum on leaving the {2_Org} in {3_Num} turns.
+1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each [ICON_RES_COAL] Coal you own (up to 10). +3% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production. European nations owning Coal may join. Merges into the European Economic Community.

Proposed by Robert Schuman in 1950 to make war between France and Germany "not merely unthinkable, but materially impossible", the Treaty of Paris (1951) pooled the coal and steel of France, West Germany, Italy and the Benelux countries.

Open borders between member civilizations. +3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each of your trade routes to another member. +5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +1 Influence per turn with each member City-State. Founded by a member of the Coal and Steel Community, which merges into it.
The Treaties of Rome (1957) created a customs union and common market among the six members of the Coal and Steel Community.

Open borders between member civilizations. Members cannot declare war on each other (leave first). +4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each of your trade routes to another member. +5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold and +5% [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. +1 Delegate in the World Congress. +2 Influence per turn with each member City-State. Founded by a member of the Economic Community, which merges into it.

The Maastricht Treaty (1993) founded the European Union, adding a common foreign and security policy, cooperation in justice and home affairs, and the path to a single currency. In 2020 the United Kingdom became the first member state to leave.
+2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Around 2100 BC Ur-Nammu of Ur took the title "King of Sumer and Akkad", claiming all of southern Mesopotamia. Later kings, those of Babylon among them, kept the style for well over a thousand years.
+2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In 1397 Queen Margaret I had her great-nephew Eric of Pomerania crowned at Kalmar as king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Sweden broke away for good under Gustav Vasa in 1523.
+10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of military units. +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Gustavus Adolphus took Riga in 1621. For a century Sweden was the great power of the Baltic, until the Great Northern War ended in 1721 with Livonia ceded to Russia.
Peter I took Riga in 1710 and, after the Treaty of Nystad brought him the Baltic coast in 1721, was proclaimed emperor of all Russia.

After King Sebastian fell in Morocco in 1578 and his successor died without heirs, Philip II of Spain claimed the Portuguese crown in 1580. Both kingdoms shared a king, but kept separate governments, until the restoration of 1640.

The Congress of Vienna joined the northern Netherlands and the former Austrian Netherlands under King William I in 1815. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 split them again; the Netherlands recognised Belgium in 1839.
On 17 March 1861, after the campaigns of Cavour and Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed King of Italy. Venice joined in 1866 and Rome, the capital, in 1870.
Kublai Khan proclaimed the Great Yuan in 1271 and completed the conquest of the Song in 1279, ruling from Khanbaliq, today's Beijing, until the Ming drove the dynasty north in 1368.

[COLOR_YELLOW]Alliance:[ENDCOLOR] a defence pact with written terms. Members cannot fight each other; when war comes, its charter decides who must answer the call to arms. Answering or refusing moves a member's credibility, and with it the alliance's cohesion.
[ICON_BULLET]Collective defence: an attack on one member is an attack on all.
[ICON_BULLET]Full alliance: members also join each other's wars of aggression.
[ICON_BULLET]Consultation: members are called to arms but may refuse without penalty.
[ICON_BULLET]Scope: home region only (aggressors whose capital lies within {1_Num} tiles of the attacked member's).
[ICON_BULLET]No separate peace while the attacked member still fights.
[ICON_BULLET]Members may make peace on their own.
[ICON_BULLET]Defence target: keep your military at {1_Num}% of the members' average or lose cohesion.
[ICON_BULLET]Tribute: members pay the leader {2_Num} [ICON_GOLD] Gold x (era + 1) per turn.
[ICON_BULLET]Leading power: the leader's own wars call members in, and members can leave only by referendum.
[ICON_BULLET]Members cannot declare war on each other.

Willing founding members now: {1_Num} (needs {2_Need}, including you). AI leaders join if they are your friends, share your ideology or faith, or face the same stronger neighbour; City-States join if they are your Friends. Click a term to change it.
Draft an alliance of your own
Name it and set its terms: what members owe each other in war, where the pact applies, whether peace must be made together, how the burden is shared, and whether one power leads.
[COLOR_GREY]Under a leading power, members can leave only by referendum.[ENDCOLOR]
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Call to arms against {1_Enemy}.[ENDCOLOR] Answer within {2_Num} turns; silence counts as refusal.
{1_Member} invokes the {2_Org} against {3_Enemy}. Answer the call to arms on the Organisations tab of Formable Nations.
{1_Member} has refused the call to arms of the {2_Org} to defend {3_Ally}.
Credibility (calls to arms answered or refused)

Founded in 478 BC on Delos to continue the war against Persia, the league's members paid tribute into a common treasury. Athens moved it to Athens in 454 BC, and the alliance became an Athenian empire.

Formed in 1167 by the communes of northern Italy to defend their liberties against Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, whom they defeated at Legnano in 1176. The Peace of Constance (1183) confirmed their rights.

Pope Pius V joined Spain, Venice and other Catholic states in 1571; their fleet won at Lepanto that October. Venice made a separate peace in 1573. A second Holy League of 1684 joined the Empire, Poland-Lithuania and Venice, later Russia.
A secret defensive alliance concluded in 1882 by Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy. Italy stayed neutral in 1914 and joined the other side in 1915.

Not a formal alliance but an understanding: the Franco-Russian Alliance (1894), the Entente Cordiale (1904) and the Anglo-Russian Convention (1907). Britain's obligations to France were never written down.

Signed in Washington in 1949. Article 5 makes an armed attack against one member an attack against them all; Article 6 limits it to the members' territory in Europe and North America. Members have agreed to spend 2% of GDP on defence.
Signed in Warsaw in 1955 by the Soviet Union and seven states of Central and Eastern Europe under a unified command led from Moscow. Albania left in 1968; the pact was dissolved in 1991.

The Abbasids took the caliphate in 750, and in 762 al-Mansur founded Baghdad, the Round City. Under Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun its House of Wisdom gathered and translated the learning of Greece, Persia and India.
+10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of military units. +2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.

From the late 10th century BC the kings of Assur built the largest empire the Near East had yet seen; the Phoenician cities paid them tribute. At Nineveh, Ashurbanipal gathered a library of thousands of clay tablets.
+5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +15% yields from internal trade routes (the Royal Road). +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Cyrus the Great entered Babylon in 539 BC. His successors ruled from the Aegean to the Indus, joined by the Royal Road from Sardis to Susa, along which couriers crossed the empire in about a week.

Carthage, founded by settlers from Tyre (by tradition in 814 BC), sent an annual offering to the temple of Melqart in its mother city for centuries, and came to lead the Phoenician world after Tyre's decline.
+5% [ICON_PEACE] Faith. +3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Justinian I set out to restore the empire of the Caesars. Belisarius took Carthage from the Vandals in 533 and entered Rome in 536; by 554 Italy was Roman again.
+10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of military units. +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
At its height in 1812, Napoleon's Grand Empire joined France to a ring of satellite states: the Confederation of the Rhine, the Kingdom of Italy, the Swiss Confederation and the Duchy of Warsaw.
United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
The Portuguese court fled to Rio de Janeiro in 1807. In 1815 the Prince Regent raised Brazil to a kingdom equal with Portugal; the union ended when Brazil declared independence in 1822.
+2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold and +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.

In 1336 the minister Gajah Mada swore the Palapa oath to unite Nusantara. The court poem Nagarakretagama (1365) lists tributaries across the archipelago and the Malay peninsula, Temasek (Singapore) among them.
+5% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.

From 1351 to 1767 the kings of Ayutthaya claimed overlordship of the Malay sultanates to the south, which sent them the bunga mas, the golden flowers of tribute; early Malacca was among them before it turned to Ming China.
Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur sent an army across the Sahara under Judar Pasha. At Tondibi in 1591 its muskets defeated the Songhai, and Gao and Timbuktu fell to Morocco.
On 29 May 1453 Mehmed II took Constantinople, made it his capital and styled himself Kayser-i Rum, Caesar of Rome.
Venice's maritime state: a third of Tyre from 1124, Ragusa from 1205 to 1358, and after the Fourth Crusade Crete and the ports of the Aegean, a chain of bases guarding the trade route to the Levant.
+2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn for each of your trade routes to another member. +2 Influence per turn with each member City-State. Only China can found it; it ends after the Industrial Era.
For two thousand years, rulers from Korea and Vietnam to Siam and Malacca sent tribute missions to the Chinese court, receiving investiture, gifts and the right to trade in return.
Founded at Belgrade in 1961 under Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah by states that would join neither bloc of the Cold War.
From 1677 a series of treaties bound the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and the English colonies, renewed at councils in Albany, where the chain of friendship was said to be polished each time.
Seat of the poet-king Nezahualcoyotl and a centre of law and learning, Texcoco joined Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan in the Triple Alliance of 1428.
A Tepanec city on the western shore of Lake Texcoco, the third and smallest partner of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
Capital of the Chimu kingdom on the Peruvian coast and the largest adobe city of the Americas, brought into the Inca realm around 1470.
High in the northern Andes, Quito became the second capital of the Inca under Huayna Capac.
The great city of northern Yucatan, crowned by the pyramid of Kukulcan, where the equinox sun draws a serpent down the stairway.
A city of the Puuc hills renowned for its stone mosaics and the Pyramid of the Magician.
Capital of Silla for nearly a thousand years, with its royal tombs and the Cheomseongdae observatory. Its last king surrendered peacefully to Goryeo in 935.
Capital of Later Baekje under Gyeon Hwon, in the fertile southwest of the peninsula; its defeat in 936 completed Goryeo's unification.
Castle town of the Satsuma domain and its Shimazu lords, at the far south of Kyushu.
Castle town of the Choshu domain, home of the academy where many leaders of the Meiji Restoration studied.
On the island of Maui, Lahaina was the royal capital of the Kingdom of Hawaii from 1820 to 1845.
Chief town of Kauai, whose ruler Kaumualii accepted Kamehameha as his sovereign by agreement in 1810.
Seat of the Scindia, one of the great houses of the Maratha Confederacy, beneath its hilltop fortress.
Capital of the Gaekwad rulers of Gujarat, a Maratha house known for its trade and patronage.
Capital of the Holkar rulers, made famous by Queen Ahilyabai, who rebuilt temples across India.
Royal city of the Zagwe dynasty, famed for its churches hewn whole from the living rock.
A walled trading city of the eastern highlands with its own emirs, a centre of Islamic learning, joined to Ethiopia in 1887.
Where the Niger meets the Sahara: a city of caravans and of the Sankore scholars, taken by Sunni Ali of Songhai in 1468.
Royal seat of the princes of Gwynedd on Anglesey, the heart of independent medieval Wales.
Historic capital of Cornouaille in Brittany, where a Breton-speaking culture endured for centuries.
Master of the isthmus between two seas, Corinth grew rich on trade; the Hellenic League was founded there in 337 BC.
A seafaring polis between Athens and Corinth, mother city of Byzantium and of colonies around the Black Sea.
Capital of the Republic of Texas from 1839, which joined the United States in 1845.
A city of Kush at the foot of the sacred mountain Jebel Barkal, the southern limit of Egypt's New Kingdom.
City-states of the Valley of Mexico
+2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In 1428 Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan formed the Excan Tlahtoloyan, the Triple Alliance that ruled central Mexico until 1521.
Tawantinsuyu, "the four parts together": under Pachacuti and his successors the Inca joined the Andes from Quito to Chile in a single state bound by roads, storehouses and the labour tax.
+2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Later chronicles tell of a league in which Mayapan, Chichen Itza and Uxmal shared rule over northern Yucatan, until Mayapan fell around 1450.
+5% [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. +2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Wang Geon founded Goryeo in 918. Silla submitted peacefully in 935 and Later Baekje fell in 936, reuniting the peninsula under a dynasty that would give Korea its name.
+2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In 1866, brokered by Sakamoto Ryoma, the rival domains of Satsuma and Choshu made a secret alliance against the shogunate.
+5% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +5% [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. +10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production of military units.
The Meiji Restoration of 1868 returned rule to the emperor. In 1871 the domains were abolished and replaced by prefectures, and the constitution of 1889 established the Empire of Japan.
+5% [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Kamehameha I united the islands between 1795 and 1810, when Kaumualii of Kauai accepted his rule by agreement. The kingdom lasted until 1893.
+2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In the 18th century the great Maratha houses, the Scindia of Gwalior, the Holkar of Indore and the Gaekwad of Baroda among them, ruled much of India as a confederacy under the Peshwa at Pune.
In 1270 Yekuno Amlak overthrew the Zagwe kings of Lalibela and founded the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba and reigned until 1974.
Menelik II, emperor from 1889, joined Harar and the southern lands to his realm. His victory at Adwa in 1896 preserved Ethiopia's independence.
Sunni Ali took Timbuktu in 1468. Under Askia Muhammad, from 1493, Songhai became the largest empire in West African history, with Timbuktu as its city of learning.
+2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
In 1401 Owain Glyndwr wrote to the King of Scots and the lords of Ireland, appealing to their common descent to stand together with the Welsh.
+1 Delegate in the World Congress. +5% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
After Chaeronea, Philip II of Macedon gathered the Greek states at Corinth in 337 BC into a league that kept the common peace and chose him its leader.
The Republic of Texas, independent from Mexico since 1836, was admitted to the United States in December 1845.
+5% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital.
Under Thutmose III, around 1450 BC, Egypt's rule reached Napata and the holy mountain of Jebel Barkal, and Kush was governed by a viceroy for the pharaoh.
